ConnectionStrings._comment: Leave these two blank here. Supply real values via environment variables (ConnectionStrings__MySql, ConnectionStrings__Redis) or a secrets manager — never commit a production connection string.

Encryption._comment: Generated for this deployment with `openssl rand -base64 32`. This is real committed key material — see the note at the bottom of this file about that tradeoff. It decrypts every user's birth data (see backend/README.md's 'Birth data encryption' section); rotating it later re-encrypts nothing automatically, so changing it makes existing rows undecryptable.

Jwt._comment: SigningKey generated with `openssl rand -base64 32`. Issuer is this deployment's real domain; Audience identifies the mobile app itself, not a domain, so it's left as-is.

Firebase._comment: Not something I can generate — needs a real Firebase project's service account JSON, placed on the production host (or mounted secret) and pointed to here, e.g. /etc/secrets/firebase-service-account.json. Until it's set, /auth/session fails with a clear 503 instead of accepting unverified tokens; that's fine while Auth:DevModeEnabled below covers login.

GooglePlaces._comment: Not something I can generate — needs a real Google Cloud API key (Places + Time Zone APIs enabled). Until set, /places/* fails with a clear error instead of silently misbehaving.

Auth._comment: Intentionally true on this deployment: real Firebase auth isn't wired up yet, so POST /auth/dev-login (OTP '123456', any phone number) is the only way in. Program.cs no longer hard-blocks this outside Development, but does log a loud warning on every startup. Set back to false the moment Firebase:CredentialsPath above is filled in. Three demo accounts (phone numbers +919999900001/2/3, one per subscription tier) are pre-seeded — see AppDbContext.cs's dev-login demo accounts comment.

Cors._comment: Origins allowed to call this API from a browser. Native iOS/Android app builds aren't affected by CORS. trafficjam-live.kaizeninfotech.com is the API's own domain, included here in case the admin panel (or a Flutter web build) is served from it too, e.g. same domain via a different path or a proxy. If the admin panel actually ends up on a separate subdomain instead, add that origin here too.

_secretsNote: Encryption:Key and Jwt:SigningKey above are real generated secrets, committed directly in this file rather than sourced from env vars/a secrets manager — a deliberate exception to the usual rule, at the user's explicit request. If this repo (or its git history) is ever exposed, both keys are compromised: birth data becomes decryptable and JWTs forgeable. Rotate both (regenerate + redeploy) before treating this as a real production posture, and prefer moving them to real secrets management once the deployment target is settled.
